job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

response.passage: Dear Diary, today in Science class, our teacher explained that our body needs a variety of nutrients to stay healthy. I learned that proteins are essential for everyone, not just bodybuilders, because they help repair our tissues and support growth. We also discussed fats; while too much is unhealthy, our bodies actually need some fat to store energy, so we shouldn't cut them out entirely. I was surprised to learn that the iron in our spinach is a tiny mineral our blood needs, not the same hard metal used to make nails! We also talked about how to prepare food properly. My mother often washes vegetables after cutting them, but the teacher said this washes away important vitamins and minerals, so we must wash them before chopping. Finally, we learned that deficiency diseases, like scurvy caused by a lack of Vitamin C, are not contagious. You cannot catch them from someone coughing near you, as they only happen when your diet lacks specific nutrients for a long time. It is important to eat a balanced diet, which means eating the right proportions of nutrients based on what our body needs, rather than just eating equal amounts of everything. I feel much more informed about how to keep my body strong and healthy!
response.summary: This diary entry explains the importance of proteins, fats, and minerals for the human body. It also clarifies common myths about food preparation, the nature of deficiency diseases, and the true meaning of a balanced diet.
